answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the lotus schedule in the pulse ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the nadir checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 4 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 33 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale. That is 34 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
